0.long_answer: Vitamin A is the essential nutrient that, when metabolized into its active form retinal, combines with the protein opsin to form rhodopsin. Rhodopsin is a photopigment found in the rod cells of the retina, which is essential for vision, especially in low-light conditions and contributes to color vision. A deficiency in vitamin A leads to an inadequate production of rhodopsin, which can result in visual impairments such as night blindness and disturbances in color perception.
